digest.component_or_area: CI test suite (mirror sweep tier) + import portability + network mocking
propositions: Four modules contain unconditional module-top `import fcntl` statements that block collection on non-POSIX platforms; `import rebar` transitively fails on Windows sweep tier with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'`.

The autouse network guard in `tests/conftest.py` patches `socket.socket.connect` for all address families, blocking AF_UNIX local IPC used by Python 3.14's forkserver multiprocessing start method, causing test failures with `RuntimeError: Network access is forbidden`.

The four unconditional fcntl imports must be guarded using module-top `try/except ImportError → fcntl = None` pattern to match existing codebase invariant; collectability must succeed on non-POSIX (Windows locking support out of scope).

The `socket.connect` guard must be narrowed to block only AF_INET/AF_INET6 (real network) and delegate other families to the captured original connect; `socket.create_connection` guard remains unchanged.

A structural AST-based linter (`scripts/check_fcntl_import_guard.py`) must detect and fail unconditional module-top fcntl imports while allowing three legitimate guard shapes (try/except, sys.platform conditional, function-local).
